events.title: Grounded spec built
events.reasoning: The product’s catalog and PRD confirm that Procol can create multi‑stage sourcing events (RFP/RFQ/auction), invite vendors, manage teams, and award contracts, so the core workflow is covered. However, the PRD specifies that the phone field must accept any 10‑digit number, while the backend only checks length, not that the characters are digits. This mismatch creates a spec‑vs‑product gap that could let invalid phone entries pass validation. Testing this validation logic will verify whether the implementation meets the documented requirement.

deltas.prdSays: Accept any 10-digit number; reject malformed input politely (PRD §4.3, §5).
deltas.productDoes: The API checks phone LENGTH (rejects 9 or 11 digits) but NOT that characters are digits — it accepts a 10-char value containing letters. The frontend enforces digits-only, so the API is more lenient than the UI.

events.title: 6 cases (LLM (Groq, RAG-grounded))
events.reasoning: I designed 6 detailed test case(s) this pass (LLM (Groq, RAG-grounded)) covering functional, data-validation, edge for 1 flow(s). Each has preconditions, numbered steps, positive/negative test data, and a precise expected result. Total so far: 6 cases across 3 dimension(s).

cases.scenario: Create RFP+RFQ event, place surrogate bid, open award proposal
cases.preconditions: Buyer is logged in with permission to create events; config switch trade:create_record is enabled.
steps: 1. Navigate to Create Event page and select event type "RFP + RFQ".
2. Fill mandatory fields: title = "Q4 Office Supplies", bid_window.start = "2026-10-01T09:00:00Z", bid_window.end = "2026-10-05T17:00:00Z".
3. Add two line items: {product: "Printer Paper", quantity: 500}, {product: "Ink Cartridge", quantity: 200}.
4. Verify that two stages are auto‑created: Technical (RFP) and Pricing (RFQ).
5. Invite vendors 101 and 102 as the audience.
7. In the vendor list, choose vendor 101 and click "Place Surrogate Bid".
8. Enter surrogate bid details: price = 1500, comments = "Internal quote" and submit.
9. Return to the event and click "Create Award Proposal".
10. Confirm proposal creation and submit for approval.
cases.testData: Positive: All fields populated as described above.
cases.expectedResult: Event is created with status "Published"; both RFP and RFQ stages are persisted in the database (trade:create_record confirmed). Two line items are stored with correct quantities. Surrogate bid record exists linked to vendor 101 and event. Award proposal record is created with status "Open" and linked to the event. No error messages are shown.

cases.preconditions: Buyer is on the Create Event form with all other required fields filled.
steps: 2. Fill bid window, add at least one line item with quantity > 0, and invite a vendor.
cases.expectedResult: Publish is blocked and the UI shows error message "Title is required". No event record is written to the database.

cases.scenario: Create line item with zero quantity
cases.preconditions: Buyer is on the Create Event form.
steps: 2. Set bid window start/end to future dates.
3. Add a line item: product = "Stapler", quantity = 0.
cases.expectedResult: Validation error displayed: "Quantity must be greater than 0". Event is not persisted.

cases.scenario: Bid end time earlier than bid start time
cases.preconditions: Buyer is creating a new event.
cases.expectedResult: Publish blocked with error "Bid end must be after bid start". No database entry created.

cases.scenario: Attempt to publish event with bid window already elapsed
steps: 3. Set bid_window.end = "2026-11-25T17:00:00Z" (both dates in the past).
4. Add at least one valid line item.
cases.testData: Negative: bid window dates are in the past.
cases.expectedResult: System returns error "Bid window must be in the future" and prevents publishing. No event record is stored.

cases.scenario: Create event with maximum allowed line items and large quantities
cases.preconditions: Buyer has permission to create events; trade:create_record enabled.
steps: 3. Add 500 line items, each with product name "ItemX" where X is 1‑500, and quantity = 2147483647 (max 32‑bit integer).
cases.testData: Positive: large number of line items and max integer quantity.
cases.expectedResult: Event is created successfully; all 500 line items are persisted with exact quantities; both RFP and RFQ stages are stored (DB‑verified). No truncation or overflow errors. System returns success message "Event published successfully".
